subject: maths
title: Percentages of Quantities: Fractions, Decimals and Discounts
seo_title: Year 6 Percentages of Quantities Worksheets: 35% of 80, 3/4 of 60 and 20% Off Sale Prices
standard_text: Solve problems that require finding a familiar fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity, including percentage discounts, choosing efficient calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: find a fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity (3/4 of 60, 0.2 of 45, 35% of 80), work out discounts and sale prices, and compare deals. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_sub: For a fraction, divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator: 3/4 of 60 = 15 × 3 = 45. For a discount, take it off the price: 20% off $45 = $45 − $9 = $36.
body_html:
A fraction of a quantity

To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.

Example

Find 34 of 60.

60 ÷ 4 = 15, so one quarter is 15. Three quarters is 3 × 15.

Answer: 45

A percentage of a quantity

Per cent means “out of 100”. Learn these four, then build any percentage from them.

PercentageFractionDecimalHow to find it
50%120.5÷ 2
25%140.25÷ 4
10%1100.1÷ 10
1%11000.01÷ 100
Example

Find 35% of 80.

10% of 80 = 8, so 30% = 24. 5% is half of 10% = 4. 35% = 24 + 4.

Answer: 28

Example

Find 99% of 300.

1% of 300 = 3. 99% = 100% − 1% = 300 − 3.

Answer: 297

A decimal of a quantity

A decimal is another way to write a fraction: 0.2 = 210 = 20%. Use whichever is easiest.

Example

Find 0.2 of 45.

0.1 of 45 = 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. 0.2 is 2 × 4.5.

Answer: 9

Discounts and sale prices

A discount is the money taken off. Find the discount, then take it away from the price.

Example

Runners cost $45. They are 20% off. What is the sale price?

10% of $45 = $4.50, so 20% = $9 off. $45 − $9.

Answer: $36

To compare deals, work out the price you pay for each one. A calculator is useful for awkward amounts, but familiar percentages are quicker in your head.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
20% off $45 = $45 − $20 = $2520% is not $20. 20% of $45 = $9, so $45 − $9 = $36
20% off $45 costs $9$9 is the discount. Take it off: $45 − $9 = $36
1% of 600 = 601% is 1100, so ÷ 100: 6. 60 is 10%
34 of 60 = 60 ÷ 3 × 4 = 80Divide by the denominator: 60 ÷ 4 × 3 = 45
0.2 of 45 = half of 450.2 is 15, not 12: 45 ÷ 5 = 9

faq.q: How do you find a percentage of a quantity in Year 6?
faq.a: Find 10% by dividing by 10 and 1% by dividing by 100, then build the percentage you need. For example, 35% of 80 is 30% (24) plus 5% (4), which makes 28.

faq.q: How do you work out 20% off a price?
faq.a: Find 20% of the price, then take it away. For $45: 10% is $4.50, so 20% is $9, and the sale price is $45 − $9 = $36.

faq.q: How do you find a fraction of an amount, like 3/4 of 60?
faq.a: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 and 15 × 3 = 45.

faq.q: Can Year 6 students use a calculator for percentages?
faq.a: Yes, the Australian Curriculum (AC9M6N07) says to use digital tools where appropriate, but students should find familiar fractions, decimals and percentages such as 50%, 25%, 10% and 1% mentally.

items.q: The bar shows 28 split into 4 equal parts. What is 14 of 28?
items.e: To find 14, divide by 4: 28 ÷ 4 = 7. 27 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 112 multiplies by 4. 14 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 21 is the other 34.

items.q: What is 13 of 27?
items.e: To find 13, divide by 3: 27 ÷ 3 = 9. 26 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 81 multiplies by 3. 13 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 18 is the other 23.

items.q: What is 110 of 90?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 89 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 900 multiplies by 10. 110 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 81 is the other 910.

items.q: What is 18 of 96?
items.e: To find 18, divide by 8: 96 ÷ 8 = 12. 95 takes away 1 instead of finding a fraction. 768 multiplies by 8. 18 of a number is smaller than the number, so divide. 84 is the other 78.

items.q: The bar shows 60 split into 4 equal parts. What is 34 of 60?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 14 of 60 is 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so 34 is 3 × 15 = 45. 15 is only 14. Multiply by 3 as well. 80 divides by the numerator (3) instead of the denominator (4). 57 takes away 3 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: The bar shows 35 split into 5 equal parts. What is 25 of 35?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 15 of 35 is 35 ÷ 5 = 7, so 25 is 2 × 7 = 14. 7 is only 15. Multiply by 2 as well. 21 is the other 35. 33 takes away 2 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 23 of 45?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 13 of 45 is 45 ÷ 3 = 15, so 23 is 2 × 15 = 30. 15 is only 13. Multiply by 2 as well. 43 takes away 2 instead of finding a fraction. 90 multiplies by 2 but forgets to divide by 3.

items.q: What is 35 of 40?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 15 of 40 is 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so 35 is 3 × 8 = 24. 8 is only 15. Multiply by 3 as well. 16 is the other 25. 37 takes away 3 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 910 of 50?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 110 of 50 is 50 ÷ 10 = 5, so 910 is 9 × 5 = 45. 5 is only 110. Multiply by 9 as well. 41 takes away 9 instead of finding a fraction. 450 multiplies by 9 but forgets to divide by 10.

items.q: What is 310 of 120?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 110 of 120 is 120 ÷ 10 = 12, so 310 is 3 × 12 = 36. 12 is only 110. Multiply by 3 as well. 84 is the other 710. 400 divides by the numerator (3) instead of the denominator (10).

items.q: What is 710 of 200?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 110 of 200 is 200 ÷ 10 = 20, so 710 is 7 × 20 = 140. 20 is only 110. Multiply by 7 as well. 60 is the other 310. 193 takes away 7 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 45 of 75?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 15 of 75 is 75 ÷ 5 = 15, so 45 is 4 × 15 = 60. 15 is only 15. Multiply by 4 as well. 71 takes away 4 instead of finding a fraction. 300 multiplies by 4 but forgets to divide by 5.

items.q: What is 58 of 64?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 18 of 64 is 64 ÷ 8 = 8, so 58 is 5 × 8 = 40. 8 is only 18. Multiply by 5 as well. 24 is the other 38. 59 takes away 5 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 56 of 42?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 16 of 42 is 42 ÷ 6 = 7, so 56 is 5 × 7 = 35. 7 is only 16. Multiply by 5 as well. 37 takes away 5 instead of finding a fraction. 210 multiplies by 5 but forgets to divide by 6.

items.q: What is 34 of 240?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 14 of 240 is 240 ÷ 4 = 60, so 34 is 3 × 60 = 180. 60 is only 14. Multiply by 3 as well. 320 divides by the numerator (3) instead of the denominator (4). 237 takes away 3 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: What is 38 of 400?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 18 of 400 is 400 ÷ 8 = 50, so 38 is 3 × 50 = 150. 50 is only 18. Multiply by 3 as well. 250 is the other 58. 397 takes away 3 instead of finding a fraction.

items.q: Which calculation finds 34 of 60?
items.e: Divide by the denominator (4) to find one quarter, then multiply by the numerator (3): 60 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15 × 3 = 45. 60 ÷ 3 × 4 = 80 mixes up the numerator and the denominator.

items.q: What is 34 of 1 hour? Give your answer in minutes.
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so 34 of an hour is 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. 15 minutes is only 14. An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so it is not 75. Divide by 4, not by 3.

items.q: What is 25 of 1 kg? Give your answer in grams.
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 ÷ 5 = 200, so 25 is 2 × 200 = 400 g. 200 g is only 15. 600 g is the other 35. 40 g has the wrong place value.

items.q: Which is more: 23 of 30 or 34 of 24?
items.e: 23 of 30: 30 ÷ 3 × 2 = 20. 34 of 24: 24 ÷ 4 × 3 = 18. 20 > 18, so 23 of 30 is more, even though 34 is the bigger fraction.

items.q: The bar shows 70 split into ten equal parts. What is 10% of 70?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 70 ÷ 10 = 7. 0.7 would be 1% (÷ 100). Do not take away 10, and do not multiply by 10.

items.q: What is 50% of 86?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 86 ÷ 2 = 43. Halve, do not double. Do not take away 50. 8.6 is only 10%.

items.q: What is 25% of 64?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 64 ÷ 4 = 16. 48 is the other 75%. Do not take away 25, and do not divide by 25.

items.q: What is 10% of 350?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 350 ÷ 10 = 35. 3.5 is only 1%. 315 is the other 90%. Do not take away 10.

items.q: What is 1% of 600?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 600 ÷ 100 = 6. 1% is a hundredth, not a tenth: 60 would be 10%. Do not take away 1. 594 is the other 99%.

items.q: What is 1% of 2500?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 2500 ÷ 100 = 25. 250 would be 10%, because 1% means ÷ 100, not ÷ 10. Do not take away 1.

items.q: The bar shows 120 split into four equal parts. What is 25% of 120?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 120 ÷ 4 = 30. 90 is the other 75%. Do not take away 25, and do not divide by 25.

items.q: What is 50% of 7?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5. The answer does not have to be a whole number. Not 7 ÷ 50. 0.7 is only 10%.

items.q: What is 1% of 45?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 45 ÷ 100 = 0.45. 4.5 would be 10%: 1% means ÷ 100. Do not take away 1. 44.55 is the other 99%.

items.q: What is 20% of 45?
items.e: 10% of 45 is 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. 20% = 2 × 4.5 = 9. 4.5 is only 10%. Do not take away 20, and do not divide by 20.

items.q: What is 30% of 250?
items.e: 10% of 250 is 250 ÷ 10 = 25. 30% = 3 × 25 = 75. 25 is only 10%. 175 is the other 70%. Do not take away 30.

items.q: The bar shows 80 split into ten parts of 10%. What is 35% of 80?
items.e: 10% of 80 is 80 ÷ 10 = 8. 30% = 3 × 8 = 24. 5% is half of 10%: 4. 35% = 30% + 5% = 24 + 4 = 28. 24 is only 30%: add the 5% as well. 52 is the other 65%. Do not take away 35.

items.q: What is 5% of 240?
What is 75% of 36?
What is 15% of 60?
What is 2% of 350?
items.e: 1% is 350 ÷ 100 = 3.5, so 2% = 2 × 3.5 = 7. 70 would be 20%: 1% is ÷ 100, not ÷ 10. 3.5 is only 1%. Do not take away 2.

items.q: What is 45% of 120?
What is 99% of 300?
What is 12% of 300?
Which calculation finds 1% of 700?
items.e: 1% is one hundredth, so divide by 100: 700 ÷ 100 = 7. 700 ÷ 10 = 70 is 10%, not 1%.

items.q: What is 0.5 of 30?
items.e: 0.5 = 12, so divide by 2: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. 60 doubles instead of halving. 6 is 30 ÷ 5, but 0.5 is a half, not a fifth. 25 takes away 5.

items.q: What is 0.1 of 70?
items.e: 0.1 = 110, so divide by 10: 70 ÷ 10 = 7. 0.7 would be 0.01 of 70. Do not take away 0.1.

items.q: What is 0.2 of 45?
items.e: 0.2 = 15, so divide by 5: 45 ÷ 5 = 9. 0.2 is one fifth, not one half. 225 is 45 ÷ 0.2, not 0.2 of 45. 4.5 is only 0.1.

items.q: What is 0.25 of 48?
items.e: 0.25 = 14, so divide by 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. 24 is 0.5 of 48. 192 is 48 × 4. 36 is 0.75 of 48.

items.q: What is 0.75 of 40?
items.e: 0.75 = 34. 40 ÷ 4 = 10, and 3 × 10 = 30. 10 is only 0.25 and 20 is 0.5. 0.75 is less than 1, so the answer must be less than 40, not 300.

items.q: What is 0.01 of 600?
items.e: 0.01 = 1100, so divide by 100: 600 ÷ 100 = 6. 60 would be 0.1 of 600. 0.6 is 0.001 of 600. 594 is 0.99 of 600.

items.q: What is 0.3 of 50?
items.e: 0.3 = 3 tenths. 0.1 of 50 is 50 ÷ 10 = 5, so 0.3 is 3 × 5 = 15. 5 is only 0.1. 35 is 0.7. 0.3 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 50, not 150.

items.q: What is 0.6 of 25?
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths. 0.1 of 25 is 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5, so 0.6 is 6 × 2.5 = 15. 2.5 is only 0.1. 10 is 0.4. 150 forgets the decimal point: 0.6 is not 6.

items.q: What is 0.05 of 80?
items.e: 0.05 is half of 0.1. 0.1 of 80 is 8, so 0.05 of 80 is 4. 0.05 is not 0.5: 40 would be 0.5 of 80. 8 is 0.1 of 80.

items.q: What is 0.4 of 120?
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths. 0.1 of 120 is 120 ÷ 10 = 12, so 0.4 is 4 × 12 = 48. 12 is only 0.1. 0.4 is not a quarter, so it is not 120 ÷ 4 = 30. 72 is 0.6.

items.q: What is 0.9 of 60?
items.e: 0.9 = 9 tenths. 0.1 of 60 is 60 ÷ 10 = 6, so 0.9 is 9 × 6 = 54. 6 is the 0.1 you take away. Do not take away 0.9. 66 is more than 60, but 0.9 is less than 1.

items.q: What is 0.2 of 3.5?
items.e: 0.2 = 15, so divide by 5: 3.5 ÷ 5 = 0.7. 0.2 is not a half, so it is not 1.75. 7 is 3.5 × 2: you still need to ÷ 10.

items.q: What is 0.5 of 7.4?
items.e: 0.5 = 12, so divide by 2: 7.4 ÷ 2 = 3.7. Halve, do not double. 1.48 is 7.4 ÷ 5. 0.37 has the wrong place value.

items.q: What is 0.3 of 2 kg? Give your answer in grams.
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. 0.1 of 2000 g is 200 g, so 0.3 is 3 × 200 = 600 g. 60 g has the wrong place value. 1400 g is 0.7. 300 g is 0.3 of only 1 kg.

items.q: What is 0.25 of 2 m? Give your answer in centimetres.
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. 0.25 is a quarter: 200 ÷ 4 = 50 cm. 25 cm is 0.25 of only 1 m. 150 cm is 0.75. 5 cm has the wrong place value.

items.q: What is 0.75 of 1 L? Give your answer in millilitres.
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. 0.75 = 34: 1000 ÷ 4 = 250, and 3 × 250 = 750 mL. 250 mL is only 0.25. 0.75 of 1 L is less than 1 L, so it is not 7500 mL.

items.q: What is 0.15 of 200?
Which is the same as 0.2 of 45?
items.e: 0.2 = 20100 = 20%, so 0.2 of 45 = 20% of 45 = 9. 2% would be 0.02. 0.2 is not a half. 45 ÷ 0.2 = 225 is far too big.

items.q: Which is the same as 0.25 of 80?
items.e: 0.25 = 25% = 14, so 0.25 of 80 = 14 of 80 = 20. 2.5% would be 0.025. 125 is not the same as 0.25.

items.q: Which is more: 0.3 of 70 or 0.4 of 50?
items.e: 0.3 of 70: 0.1 is 7, so 0.3 is 21. 0.4 of 50: 0.1 is 5, so 0.4 is 20. 21 > 20, so 0.3 of 70 is more, even though 0.4 is the bigger decimal.

items.q: A pair of runners costs $45. It is 20% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $45 is $45 ÷ 10 = $4.50. 20% = 2 × $4.50 = $9. That is the discount. Sale price: $45 − $9 = $36. $25 takes off $20, not 20%. $9 is only the discount. $40.50 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A school bag costs $80. It is 30% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $80 is $80 ÷ 10 = $8. 30% = 3 × $8 = $24. That is the discount. Sale price: $80 − $24 = $56. $24 is the discount, not the price. $50 takes off $30, not 30%. $72 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A cricket bat costs $60. It is 10% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: $60 ÷ 10 = $6. That is the discount. Sale price: $60 − $6 = $54. $6 is the discount. $50 takes off $10, not 10%. $59.90 takes off 10c.

items.q: A snorkel set costs $80. It is 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: $80 ÷ 4 = $20. That is the discount. Sale price: $80 − $20 = $60. $20 is the discount. $55 takes off $25, not 25%. $40 would be 50% off.

items.q: A netball costs $65. It is 20% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $65 is $65 ÷ 10 = $6.50. 20% = 2 × $6.50 = $13. That is the discount. Sale price: $65 − $13 = $52. $13 is the discount. $45 takes off $20, not 20%. $58.50 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A scooter costs $120. It is 40% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $120 is $120 ÷ 10 = $12. 40% = 4 × $12 = $48. That is the discount. Sale price: $120 − $48 = $72. $48 is the discount. $80 takes off $40, not 40%. $108 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A tablet costs $200. It is 5% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $200 is $20. 5% is half of 10%: $10. That is the discount. Sale price: $200 − $10 = $190. $10 is the discount. $195 takes off $5, not 5%. $160 takes off 200 ÷ 5 = $40, which is 20%.

items.q: A beach towel costs $16. In a clearance sale it is 75% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 50% is $16 ÷ 2 = $8. 25% is half of that: $4. 75% = 50% + 25% = $8 + $4 = $12. That is the discount. Sale price: $16 − $12 = $4. $12 is the discount. $8 is only 50% off. $15.25 takes off 75c, not 75%.

items.q: A footy jumper costs $60. It is 35% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $60 is $60 ÷ 10 = $6. 30% = 3 × $6 = $18. 5% is half of 10%: $3. 35% = 30% + 5% = $18 + $3 = $21. That is the discount. Sale price: $60 − $21 = $39. $21 is the discount. $25 takes off $35, not 35%. $42 takes off only 30%.

items.q: A board game costs $50. It is 12% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $50 is $50 ÷ 10 = $5. 1% is $50 ÷ 100 = 50c, so 2% = 2 × 50c = $1. 12% = 10% + 2% = $5 + $1 = $6. That is the discount. Sale price: $50 − $6 = $44. $6 is the discount. $38 takes off $12, not 12%. $45 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A bike helmet costs $70. It is 60% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% of $70 is $70 ÷ 10 = $7. 60% = 6 × $7 = $42. That is the discount. Sale price: $70 − $42 = $28. $42 is the discount. $10 takes off $60, not 60%. $63 takes off only 10%.

items.q: A beach umbrella costs $90. It is 30% off. How much money is taken off?
items.e: 10% of $90 is $90 ÷ 10 = $9. 30% = 3 × $9 = $27. $63 is the sale price, not the money taken off. 30% is not $30. $9 is only 10%.

items.q: A pair of swimming goggles costs $40. It is 15% off. How much money is taken off?
items.e: 10% of $40 is $40 ÷ 10 = $4. 5% is half of 10%: $2. 15% = 10% + 5% = $4 + $2 = $6. $34 is the sale price, not the money taken off. 15% is not $15. $4 is only 10%.

items.q: A lunch box costs $36. It is 13 off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 13 of $36 is $36 ÷ 3 = $12 off. Sale price: $36 − $12 = $24. $12 is the discount. $33 takes off $3, not a third. $27 takes off only a quarter.

items.q: At the school canteen a meat pie costs $4.50. On Fridays it is 10% off. What is the Friday price?
items.e: 10% of $4.50 is $4.50 ÷ 10 = 45c off. Friday price: $4.50 − 45c = $4.05. 45c is the discount. $4.40 takes off 10c, not 10%. $4.95 adds 10% instead of taking it off.

items.q: A rashie cost $50. In the sale it costs $40. What percentage has been taken off?
items.e: $10 has been taken off. 1050 = 20100 = 20%. $10 off is not 10%. 80% is the part you still pay. Compare with the old price ($50), not the new price ($40).

items.q: A frisbee cost $25. In the sale it costs $15. What percentage has been taken off?
items.e: $10 has been taken off. 1025 = 40100 = 40%. $10 off is not 10%. 60% is the part you still pay. $15 is the new price, not a percentage.

items.q: A shirt costs $30 and a cap costs $20. Everything is 25% off. How much do you pay for both?
items.e: Total before the sale: $30 + $20 = $50. 25% of $50 is $50 ÷ 4 = $12.50 off. You pay $50 − $12.50 = $37.50. $12.50 is the discount. $25 takes off $25, not 25%. $45 takes off only 10%.

items.q: Ava buys a $48 video game that is 25% off. She pays with a $50 note. How much change does she get?
items.e: 25% of $48 is $48 ÷ 4 = $12 off, so the game costs $48 − $12 = $36. Change: $50 − $36 = $14. $2 is the change without the discount. $12 is the discount. $36 is the price, not the change.

items.q: Which sale gives a price of $36?

sets.title: Compare deals and solve real-life problems

items.q: Sienna wants a $45 game. One shop offers 20% off. Another shop offers $10 off. Which is the better deal?
items.e: 20% of $45 is $9 off. $10 off saves more than $9, so $10 off is the better deal. 20% is not the same as $20 or $10.

items.q: A pair of jeans costs $36 in two shops. Shop A takes 25% off. Shop B takes $8 off. Which shop is cheaper now?
items.e: Shop A: 25% of $36 = $9 off, so $27. Shop B: $36 − $8 = $28. $27 < $28, so Shop A is cheaper.

items.q: A pair of shoes costs $60. Which saves more: 13 off or 30% off?
items.e: 13 of $60 is $20. 30% of $60 is $18. $20 > $18, so 13 off saves more. 13 is about 33%, which is more than 30%.

items.q: Shop A sells a hat for $50 with 20% off. Shop B sells the same hat for $44 with 10% off. Which shop is cheaper?
items.e: Shop A: 20% of $50 = $10 off, so $40. Shop B: 10% of $44 = $4.40 off, so $44 − $4.40 = $39.60. $39.60 < $40, so Shop B is cheaper, even though its discount is smaller.

items.q: A skateboard costs $70. Which saves more: half price or 40% off?
items.e: Half price is 50% off: $70 ÷ 2 = $35 off. 40% of $70 is $28 off. $35 > $28, so half price saves more.

items.q: Shop A sells a backpack for $80 with 25% off. Shop B sells it for $75 with $15 off. Which shop is cheaper?
items.e: Shop A: 25% of $80 = $20 off, so $60. Shop B: $75 − $15 = $60. Both cost $60, so they cost the same.

items.q: Bottles of water cost $3 each. You need 3 bottles. Which deal is cheaper: “buy 2, get 1 free” or “30% off everything”?
items.e: Buy 2, get 1 free: you pay for 2 bottles, 2 × $3 = $6. 30% off: 3 bottles cost $9, 30% of $9 is $2.70, so you pay $9 − $2.70 = $6.30. $6 < $6.30, so buy 2, get 1 free is cheaper.

items.q: A bike costs $120. Which discount saves the most money?
items.e: 25% of $120 is $30. 20% of $120 is $24. 110 of $120 is $12. $30 is more than $28, so 25% off saves the most.

items.q: There are 240 students at a school. 35% of them walk to school. How many students walk to school?
items.e: 10% of 240 is 240 ÷ 10 = 24. 30% = 3 × 24 = 72. 5% is half of 10%: 12. 35% = 30% + 5% = 72 + 12 = 84 students. 35 would be 35 out of 100, but there are 240 students. 156 is the other 65%. 72 is only 30%.

items.q: 160 students go to the swimming carnival. 34 of them swim in a race. How many students swim in a race?
items.e: Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 14 of 160 is 160 ÷ 4 = 40, so 34 is 3 × 40 = 120. 40 is only 14. Do not take away 3. 80 is a half.

items.q: A sausage sizzle has 200 sausages. By lunchtime 0.6 of them are sold. How many sausages are left?
items.e: 0.1 of 200 is 20, so 0.6 is 6 × 20 = 120 sold. Left: 200 − 120 = 80. 120 is the number sold, not left. 140 takes away 60, not 0.6. 60 thinks 0.6 means 60.

items.q: A footy stadium holds 40 000 people. It is 85% full. How many people are in the stadium?
items.e: 10% of 40 000 is 40 000 ÷ 10 = 4000. 80% = 8 × 4000 = 32 000. 5% is half of 10%: 2000. 85% = 80% + 5% = 32 000 + 2000 = 34 000. 6000 is the number of empty seats. Do not take away 85. 3400 has the wrong place value.

items.q: A cake recipe uses 250 g of sugar. Lachlan uses 40% less sugar. How much sugar does he use?
items.e: 10% of 250 g is 25 g, so 40% is 100 g. Lachlan uses 250 g − 100 g = 150 g. 100 g is the sugar left out, not the sugar used. 210 g takes away 40 g, not 40%. Less sugar, not more.

items.q: A school wants to raise $3000 for new sports equipment. So far it has raised 45% of it. How much more does it need?
items.e: 10% of $3000 is $300, so 40% is $1200, and 5% is $150. 45% = $1200 + $150 = $1350 raised. Still needed: $3000 − $1350 = $1650. $1350 is what has been raised. $2955 takes away $45, not 45%.

items.q: Charlotte has a 1.5 L bottle of water. She drinks 30% of it. How much water does she drink?
items.e: 1.5 L = 1500 mL. 10% is 150 mL, so 30% is 3 × 150 = 450 mL. 45 mL has the wrong place value. 1050 mL is what is left. Do not take away 30.

items.q: A netball team played 20 games and won 0.75 of them. How many games did the team win?
items.e: 0.75 = 34. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so 34 is 3 × 5 = 15 games. 5 is the number of games lost. 75 is not possible: the team only played 20 games. Do not take away 0.75.

items.q: Aarav gets $20 pocket money each week and saves 15% of it. How much does he save in 4 weeks?
items.e: 10% of $20 is $2 and 5% is $1, so 15% is $3 each week. In 4 weeks: 4 × $3 = $12. $3 is only one week. $68 is what he spends. $60 uses $15, not 15%.

items.q: The canteen sold 120 items at lunch. 25% were fruit cups and 13 were sushi rolls. The rest were wraps. How many wraps were sold?
items.e: Fruit cups: 25% of 120 = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. Sushi: 13 of 120 = 120 ÷ 3 = 40. Wraps: 120 − 30 − 40 = 50. 70 is the fruit cups and sushi together. 90 and 80 only take away one of them.

items.q: 90 Year 6 students are going on an excursion. On the day, 10% are away sick. How many students go on the excursion?
items.e: 10% of 90 is 90 ÷ 10 = 9 away. 90 − 9 = 81 students go. 9 is the number away. Do not take away 10 or 1.

items.q: A pair of footy boots costs $150. They are 20% off, and then a $10 voucher is taken off the sale price. How much do they cost?
items.e: 20% of $150: 10% is $15, so 20% is $30. Sale price: $150 − $30 = $120. Then the voucher: $120 − $10 = $110. $120 forgets the voucher. $40 is the total saved. $130 takes off $20, not 20%.
